kind: Read-only feasibility audit; not private-path E2E qualification
interpretation: Every observed instance has both replicas on one physical host. A local VPC would not replace an existing inter-host sibling path in this snapshot.
Co-location is an intentional controller preference; it can change during placement or evacuation, so this observation is not a permanent guarantee.
No ready off-host sibling exists for any observed instance. Sequential host restarts alone do not preserve its regional endpoint availability.
Cross-location private transport is not supplied by Vultr VPCs. A separate physical/partner interconnect requires feasibility and pricing confirmation.
Current controller publishes automatic topology only for OVH; Vultr keeps existing canonical mTLS routing.

sources.finding: Bare-metal VPC support; restart documented for cloud-init interface configuration. General API example uses instances path, while official SDK and successful live reads use bare-metals VPC endpoints.
Bare-metal VPC read and attachment paths.
VPC confined to one location; VPN gateways proposed for cross-location connectivity.
Private networks do not cross data-center locations; dedicated/partner transport is separate.
VPC interface example has MTU 1450; actual bare-metal MTU and Cilium encapsulation need measurement.

limitations: No host SSH, reboot, attachment, VPC creation, paid order or runtime change performed.
API list success does not prove attachment eligibility or data-plane connectivity.
No live Vultr MTU, source-address filtering, private-interface capture or throughput test performed.
VPC and interconnect pricing not verified; no purchase authorized by this audit.
outcome: Keep Vultr topology disabled until a useful and physically qualified path exists; do not represent a public VPN as private underlay.
